rows.evidence: joi170166supp2_prod.pdf p.5; jama_huffman_2018_oi_170166.pdf pp.3,7; joi170166supp3_prod.pdf pp.21-22 (text layer).

rows.R: Protocol p.9 §2.2.3 and SAP pp.2-3 §2.1.2 name in-hospital and 30-day 'expanded MACE' as a secondary objective; the report (pp.3,8-9; eTable 7) labels MACE+HF/shock/arrest post hoc/exploratory (disclosed). rows.evidence: joi170166supp1_prod.pdf p.9; joi170166supp2_prod.pdf pp.2-5; main pp.3,8,9; supp3 pp.1,23 (text layer).

rows.R: SAP p.7 §7.5.2 a priori subgroups: hospital size, toolkit-component use, age <65/>65, sex, STEMI/NSTEMI. Report (p.3; Figure 3 p.9) calls 'prespecified' age <50/50-69/>=70 and adds hospital type; toolkit-use subgroup not reported (process evaluation to be reported separately).
rows.evidence: joi170166supp2_prod.pdf pp.5,7; joi170166supp1_prod.pdf (searched for subgroup terms); main pp.3,9,10.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 gives two adjusted effects per time outcome: door-to-balloon difference 6.18 (-4.78 to 17.14) vs beta 13.00 (3.64-22.36); door-to-needle 0.40 vs 5.00. Column header 'Difference, %' for minutes, and fn b (logistic or quantile regression) does not say which model/estimand each column is; inference differs for D2B.
rows.evidence: jama_huffman_2018_oi_170166.pdf pp.3,6 (text layer).
rows.rationale: Both columns are labeled as adjusted for clustering and temporal trends, and footnote b describes a single family of models (marginal-effect difference from mixed logistic or quantile regression). For time outcomes the 'Difference, %' column cannot be a percentage, and the two minute-scale estimates differ by 6.8 min (D2B) and 4.6 min (D2N); the D2B beta CI excludes 0 whereas the difference CI includes 0. A legitimate explanation (marginal mean effect vs median quantile coefficient) is possible but not stated, so a reader cannot tell which value is the adjusted effect. Probable rather than confirmed because the two could be distinct valid estimands. Substantive because the conclusion about door-to-balloon time depends on which column is read. Also: the D2N beta CI is printed '−5.20-15.20' (hyphen as range separator with a negative bound).

rows.R: Supp3 p.1 index titles eFigure 1A 'Residual ... (Expected - Observed)'; p.24 caption says negative (left) residuals are hospitals with MACE lower than the mean and positive (right) higher. Under E-O a negative residual means observed above expected. The two definitions conflict; plot rendered and checked.
rows.evidence: joi170166supp3_prod.pdf p.1 (text), p.24 (rendered at 130 dpi); main p.9.
rows.rationale: If residual = expected − observed, a hospital with higher-than-expected MACE has a negative residual and would sit on the left, contradicting the caption, which places higher-MACE hospitals on the right. The page-24 title says only 'hospital residuals'; the caption describes model-based predicted rates, consistent with a random-effect/observed-minus-expected orientation. One of the two statements is wrong. Hospitals are unidentified and the display only illustrates heterogeneity, whose magnitude does not depend on the sign, so the issue is presentation-level.

rows.R: eTable 1 p.17 LDL 9.0 (3.2 to 14.8). Using header Ns (21079/295) gives 3.7-14.3 (Welch) or 4.3-13.7 (pooled), but LDL was measured in only 14830/21374 (Table 1 p.5). About 245 missing-follow-up participants with LDL reproduces the printed CI; a smaller LDL denominator explains the width.
rows.evidence: joi170166supp3_prod.pdf p.17; jama_huffman_2018_oi_170166.pdf p.5 Table 1 (text layer); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: Welch SE with n=21079/295 = 2.693 → 3.72 to 14.28; pooled SE 2.396 → 4.30 to 13.70 (matches card). With LDL availability scaled to the overall 69.4% (14830/21374), SE 3.230 → 2.67 to 15.33. Solving for the missing-group LDL n that gives half-width 5.8 (complete-group n≈14626) yields n≈245. The printed interval lies inside the plausible range once the LDL-specific denominator is recognized; Table 1 explicitly shows LDL missing for about 31% of participants, while age, weight, SBP, heart rate and hemoglobin are nearly complete, which is why those rows reproduce with header Ns. Not an issue; exclude. Outside the candidate: eTable 1 footnote a reads 'Difference = intervention minus control' but the columns are complete vs missing follow-up (signs indicate missing minus complete).

rows.R: SAP p.6 §7.2 plans complete-case and multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses for missing outcomes. Report p.7 states only that MI and hypothetical-scenario results were similar (no numbers); no complete-case analysis is identified in main text or supp3; Figure 1 says lost-to-follow-up patients were included in the analysis.
rows.evidence: joi170166supp2_prod.pdf pp.6-7; main pp.3,4,6,7; joi170166supp3_prod.pdf pp.1,17,21-23 (text layer).
rows.rationale: Searched the main article and the eTable/eFigure index: no complete-case result for 30-day MACE is presented, and the primary analysis included participants lost to follow-up (Figure 1 caption), so the primary model is not itself the complete-case analysis. The MI sensitivity is reported only qualitatively. The planned complete-case sensitivity analysis is therefore not reported. Missing outcomes were 295/21374 (1.4%), so the practical effect is likely small; L describes the analysis difference only.

rows.R: Final protocol v1.4 p.71 §4.1.1 (amendment table p.110) adds: survival with unchanged pre-randomization neurological disability counts as favorable. Article (pp.1,3,4) defines success as CPC 1-2 only, and Table 2 fn b (p.6) says CPC 1 and 2 were counted as success. Whether any CPC 3-4 survivor qualified is not reported.
rows.evidence: joi180004supp1_prod.pdf pp.15,71,110,122 (text), p.131 (OCR, signed SAP); jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf pp.1,3,4,6.
rows.rationale: The amended primary endpoint definition includes an exception for pre-existing disability; the original protocol and the SAP (native and signed) do not. The report states the CPC<=2 rule only; ITT counts reconcile with CPC1+CPC2 (35+9=44; 37+6=43). With 11 CPC 3 and 11 CPC 4 survivors in ITT, application of the exception could change the primary counts, but the materials cannot show whether it was applied. The written definitions differ for the primary outcome, so substantive_difference describes the difference; the size of any effect is unknown.

rows.R: Airway difficulty/failure/complications are secondary endpoints in protocol v1.3/v1.4 (pp.9-10,16,64-65,71) and the article (pp.1,3), and a safety-endpoint family in the SAP (p.122 §6.2). The article reports them as secondary and analyzes them in the safety (as-treated) population, consistent with both. No conflict in conduct.
rows.rationale: The report's labeling follows the protocol (secondary endpoints) and its analysis follows the SAP (adverse-event analysis on the safety population, chi-square/Fisher). Secondary and safety designations are not mutually exclusive here, and the difference lies between plan documents rather than between plan and report. Equivalent status once context is considered; exclude. Card's alternative (secondary as umbrella) matches my reading.

rows.R: SAP §5.3 and §8.2.1-8.2.4 (pp.121,124; signed pp.130,133 OCR) plan an as-treated (AT) NI analysis of the primary endpoint, secondary analyses on PP and AT, and ORs with 95% CIs for secondary and safety rates. The article and eTables report ITT/PP only, risk differences only; no AT primary analysis and no ORs. eTable 2 reclassification row is post hoc, not the AT analysis.
rows.evidence: joi180004supp1_prod.pdf pp.37,91,92,121,124 (text), 130,133 (OCR); main pp.1-9; joi180004supp2_prod.pdf pp.1-3.
rows.rationale: Searched the whole main article and the 3-page results supplement: the only reclassification analysis (eTable 2: patients intubated after BMV before ROSC counted in ETI group) is labeled post hoc and is not presented as the planned AT noninferiority analysis. Methods p.3 says ORs were calculated, but none is shown. A planned analysis population for the primary outcome is missing, so substantive_difference.

rows.R: Main p.4: 'The lower limit of the confidence interval was greater than the threshold of noninferiority, thus noninferiority was not demonstrated', but -1.64% is below -1%. Wording reverses the ordering; conclusion is correct. Recomputed ITT 44/1018 vs 43/1022: diff 0.115%, Wald lower -1.64%, Newcombe lower -1.67%; NI P one-sided = .106.
rows.evidence: jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf pp.1-4,7,8 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: p1=4.322%, p2=4.207%, RD=0.115, Wald 95% CI -1.639 to 1.868 (matches printed -1.64); Newcombe hybrid score -1.667 to 1.900; z for H0 margin -1% = 1.246, one-sided P=0.106 (printed .11). The bound lies below the margin, so the sentence's 'greater than' is wrong; the conclusion, abstract, Key Points and Discussion all say noninferiority was not shown. Presentation error only.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 PP rows. Survival at 28 d 54/995 vs 51/943: RD 0.02, Wald CI -2.00 to 2.04; printed 0.1 (-10 to 9.7). Admission 289/995 vs 312/943: RD -4.04, CI -8.16 to 0.08 (chi-square P=.055 matches); printed -4.0 (-7.6 to 0.6), not centered on the estimate. Other rows (ITT survival, admission, ROSC; PP ROSC) reproduce.
rows.evidence: jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf pp.3,6 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R Wald RD: ITT survival 0.119 (-1.83 to 2.07) printed 0.1 (-1.8 to 2.1); ITT admission -3.70 (-7.70 to 0.30) printed matches; ITT ROSC -4.66 (-8.83 to -0.49) matches; PP ROSC -5.61 (-9.91 to -1.31) matches. PP survival interval printed -10 to 9.7 is roughly five times too wide on each side; PP admission interval -7.6 to 0.6 is asymmetric about -4.0 and differs from -8.16 to 0.08. The same method reproduces every other row, so these two intervals are wrong. Inference is unchanged (all cross 0) but the printed intervals are extractable PP results, so substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 PP ROSC ETI '377 (30.0)' with n=943: 377/943 = 40.0%. Printed difference -5.6 matches 34.4-40.0, so 30.0 is a typographic error for 40.0; as printed the percentages imply BMV higher, opposite to the difference.
rows.evidence: jama_jabre_2018_oi_180004.pdf pp.4,6 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: 377/943=0.3998; 342/995=34.37%; RD -5.61 (-9.91 to -1.31), P=.011 (printed .01). The count, denominator, difference, CI and P are mutually consistent; only the ETI percentage is wrong. The correct value is recoverable, so minor_presentation; someone extracting percentages directly would take the wrong value, hence J=possible.

rows.R: Signed SAP p.130 (rendered/OCR) prints H1: piBVM - piTI >= 0.01; native SAP p.121 and protocol §11.2 (pp.36,90) print >= -0.01. H0 on the same signed page is <= -0.01 and the operational rule §8.2.1 (signed p.133) uses lower CI limit > -0.01, so intent is clear.
rows.evidence: joi180004supp1_prod.pdf p.121,124 (text), pp.130,133 (OCR 300 dpi, crop viewed), pp.36,37,90,91 (text).
rows.rationale: Real discrepancy between two copies of the same SAP: a dropped minus sign in the signed copy's H1. Within the signed copy H1 is not the complement of its own H0, and the decision rule and sample-size text use -1%. The guide's example treats a sign conflict in a margin as usually substantive, but here the operational boundary is stated correctly in the same signed document, and the report uses -1%. I judge it a typographic inconsistency whose meaning is clear (minor_presentation). Also both copies write H1 with >= rather than >, overlapping H0 at the boundary.

rows.R: eTable 2 p.3 ECMO/donation-excluded row: 43/971 vs 39/978, RD 0.44, Wald CI -1.34 to 2.22; printed 0.4 [-2.2, 1.3], which is the interval for ETI-BMV (-0.44, -2.22 to 1.34): sign-reversed. Companion row 41/863 vs 45/1174 reproduces (0.92, -0.88 to 2.71). P .63 matches.
rows.evidence: joi180004supp2_prod.pdf p.3; main pp.3,4,6 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: row 1 RD 0.441 (-1.342 to 2.223), chi-square P=0.628; reversed direction gives -0.441 (-2.223 to 1.342), matching the printed limits exactly after rounding. The printed CI therefore belongs to the opposite contrast. For a noninferiority question with margin -1%, the printed lower bound -2.2 vs correct -1.3 misstates the post hoc result, though both lie below -1%. Exclusion counts reconcile: BMV 35+12=47 (1018-971), ETI 23+21=44 (1022-978), total 91 as in text. Outside the candidate: the companion row adds 155 BMV patients to ETI (1018-863=155, matching text) but ETI n=1174 rather than 1022+155=1177; and main text p.6 calls this 'exclusion of patients intubated after BMV' while methods and eTable 2 describe reclassification to the ETI group.

rows.R: SCDE: RD -0.34 (-0.73 to 0.05) vs RR 0.77 (0.61-0.97), P=.03 (abstract p.1; p.6; Table 3 p.7). Table 3 fn a and methods p.5 state the identity-link RD for SCDE was not baseline-adjusted (nonconvergence fallback); P=.03 belongs to the baseline-adjusted Poisson RR, which agrees with it. Different models, disclosed; no CI/P conflict.
rows.evidence: jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf pp.1,5,6,7 (text).
rows.rationale: RR CI excludes 1 and P=.03 are consistent with each other; the RD CI comes from a different model (no baseline adjustment) and has no displayed P. The guide asks first whether both come from the same model; they do not, and the report says so. Exclude. Minor wording point: the abstract and text call the RD 'adjusted', which is true only for clustering, not baseline; I note it but do not consider it a reporting error of the kind flagged.

rows.R: Protocol p.16 plans analysis of the number of times all 7 items were documented (24-h frequency, p.12/p.14). Report pp.3-4 and Table 2 p.6 use the proportion of the last observation set with >=5 of 7 types. Disclosed in report pp.3-4 (revised before analyses).
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf pp.12,14,16; main pp.3,4,6; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf pp.4-5 (text).
rows.rationale: Both the unit (all sets in 24 h vs last set) and the threshold (7 vs >=5) of the documentation-completeness outcome changed. The report discloses the revision; per the fixed review decision it is retained with 'disclosed'. The measure itself changes, so substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol Table 5 p.24: circulatory SCDE requires >60 mL/kg fluid AND inotrope/vasopressor; death only on the ward. eTable 1 p.6 uses fluid >60 mL/kg 'and/or' vasoactive drug and adds death within 1 h of ICU admission; main p.4 says vasoactive 'or' fluid >=60 mL/kg and intubation in the 12 h before admission.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf pp.10,11,24; main pp.1,4,7; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf pp.6,11 (text).
rows.rationale: The planned circulatory component is a conjunction (fluid and vasoactive drug); the report uses a disjunction, which admits more events. The report adds death within the first ICU hour, and the main-text intubation window (12 h before admission) differs from the protocol (at transfer or within 1 h after). The main text (>=60) and eTable 1 (>60) also differ on the fluid boundary. Component definitions of the key secondary composite changed; substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol pp.11-12,16 lists potentially preventable cardiac arrest, hospital and PICU readmission, ICU mortality and PIM2 score as secondary outcomes/analyses. Main p.4 calls PIM2 at admission 'not prespecified', and Table 3 p.7 places these outcomes under 'Post hoc Outcomes' while p.4 calls them prespecified.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf pp.1,11,12,16; joi180015supp2_prod.pdf p.5; main pp.4,7; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf p.12 (text).
rows.rationale: Status difference between plan and report for several outcomes: prespecified in the protocol but labeled post hoc (Table 3 heading) or not prespecified (PIM2 score, main p.4). Footnote g treats them as exploratory with Holm adjustment, which may explain the 'post hoc' wording as referring to the multiplicity treatment, but the PIM2 score is explicitly named in the protocol (p.12 [5], p.16 linear model) and the report says it was not prespecified. Retained as an outcome-status difference.

rows.R: Protocol p.16: hospital-level logit regression weighted by hospital size with baseline logit and size stratum. SAP pp.1-4 and report pp.4-5: GEE binomial (exchangeable) with treatment and baseline only; stratum dropped (disclosed p.5: only 3 hospitals >=200 beds). Report matches the undated SAP, not the protocol.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.16; joi180015supp2_prod.pdf pp.1-4; main pp.4,5,7 (text).
rows.rationale: Primary analysis model changed from a weighted aggregate logit regression including the stratification variable to an unweighted GEE without strata. The removal of strata is disclosed. The SAP (undated, past tense) matches the report, so the change likely occurred before analysis, but the plan-report difference with the protocol is real and concerns the primary analysis.

rows.R: SAP pp.2-3 specifies identity-link Poisson GEE for the rate difference with the baseline rate as predictor; protocol p.16 also adjusts for baseline. Report p.5 and Table 3 fn a: SCDE RD not adjusted for baseline because the model did not converge (disclosed).
rows.evidence: joi180015supp2_prod.pdf pp.2-3; joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.16; main pp.1,5,7 (text).
rows.rationale: The absolute-effect estimate for the key secondary outcome omits the planned baseline adjustment; the report discloses the fallback rule (p.5). Retained as a disclosed analysis difference. It matters for interpretation because the unadjusted RD interval includes 0 while the adjusted RR excludes 1.

rows.R: Protocol p.16 lists 4 a priori subgroups (size, MET/RRT, ECMO, urgent ICU admission from ward); SAP p.6 plans ECMO and MET subgroup GEE interaction analyses. Report p.5 states the planned subgroup analyses are not reported (disclosed); none appear in main text or supp3.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.16; joi180015supp2_prod.pdf p.6; main pp.1-9; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf pp.1-14 (text).
rows.rationale: Planned subgroup analyses are absent; the report says so explicitly. Disclosed omission retained per fixed decision.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6 respiratory rate 0.85 (0.02 to 1.68), P=.05, Holm-adjusted P=.18. The CI and the unadjusted P are multiplicity-unadjusted (Wald check: SE 0.4235, z 2.007, P 0.045, consistent with .05 after rounding); the Holm P is a separate column. No conflict.
rows.evidence: jama_parshuram_2018_oi_180015.pdf pp.5,6 (text); hand recomputation.
rows.rationale: (1.68-0.02)/3.92 = 0.4235; 0.85/0.4235 = 2.007; two-sided P = 0.045, within rounding of printed .05 given the CI bounds' display precision. A multiplicity-adjusted P exceeding .05 alongside an unadjusted 95% CI that excludes 0 is expected; the table labels the columns separately. Exclude. The text p.6 reporting this as an increase with P=.05 is fine.

rows.R: Protocol p.16 secondary analysis (d): all-cause mortality following DNR orders with the logit model. Report gives mortality without DNR (p.6, Table 3, eTable 2) and only the count of deaths after DNR (155, p.6); limitation 6 (p.9) refers to a 'sensitivity analysis of mortality after DNR order' that is not shown.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf pp.10,16; main pp.6,7,9; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf p.9 (text).
rows.rationale: 244-42-47 = 155 deaths after DNR (matches text); BedsidePEWS 97-42=55, usual care 147-47=100. No modeled estimate for mortality following DNR is presented; the report shows the complementary subset. The protocol's broader intent (analyses with and without DNR, p.10) may be met by the non-DNR analysis, but the specifically named analysis is not reported, and the limitation's reference to it has no displayed result.

rows.R: Protocol p.12: PICU and hospital readmission expressed per 1000 hospital discharges. Table 3 p.7 fn h: ICU readmission per 1000 ICU discharges (64/1859 = 34.43 reproduces). Undated SAP p.5 shell also uses ICU discharges, so the report matches the SAP but not the protocol.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf p.12; joi180015supp2_prod.pdf p.5; main pp.5,7 (text); hand recomputation.
rows.rationale: 64/1859*1000 = 34.43 and 73/2599*1000 = 28.09 match the printed baseline rates, confirming ICU-discharge denominators. With hospital discharges the rates would be 2.40 and 1.56. The outcome's denominator (and therefore the modeled probability) differs from the protocol. The protocol sentence may be a loose summary, and the SAP may supersede it; I record the difference with that context.

rows.R: Protocol p.14 §2.11: 18% RRR = ARR 0.09%; power appendix p.29: 18% RRR 'corresponds to an absolute risk reduction of 0.9%'. With baseline 5.1/1000, 18% gives 0.92/1000 = 0.09%; the appendix's 0.9% is a unit slip. Summary p.1 and article p.4 say 0.9 per 1000.
rows.evidence: joi180015supp1_prod.pdf pp.1,14,29; main p.4 (text).
rows.rationale: 0.178*5.1 = 0.91 per 1000 = 0.091%. The body, summary and article agree on 0.9/1000; the appendix's '0.9%' is ten times too large and inconsistent with its own baseline (5.1/1000) and RRR (0.178). The design assumptions are unambiguous elsewhere in the same document, so the inconsistency is presentational.

rows.R: SAP pp.4-5 'Sensitivity to model choice' lists about 14 alternative models (GLMM, pre-post interaction, weighted linear, quasi-likelihood) for ORs, rate ratios and differences. No such results appear in the article or supp3 (eFigs 1-2, eTables 1-5).
rows.evidence: joi180015supp2_prod.pdf pp.4-5; main pp.4-7; joi180015supp3_prod.pdf pp.1-14 (text).
rows.rationale: Searched all report materials: only the primary GEE results are given; the planned model-choice sensitivity analyses are not reported or mentioned. Planned sensitivity analyses of the primary and key secondary outcomes absent.

rows.R: All 10 RRs in Table 2 (p.6; abstract p.1) reproduce as P(low group | event)/P(low group | no event), not as event-risk ratios. E.g., ARDS 17/448 vs 23/462: risk RR 0.76 (0.41-1.41); printed 0.86 (0.59-1.24) = transposed ratio 0.86 (0.59-1.24). Pneumonia printed 1.07 vs risk RR 1.15. Chi-square P values are unaffected.
rows.evidence: jama_simonis_2018_oi_180108.pdf pp.1,4,6 (text); R recomputation of all 10 rows.
rows.rationale: R (Wald log-scale): ICU mortality risk RR 1.17 (0.94-1.45) vs transposed 1.11 (0.96-1.28), printed 1.11 (0.96-1.27); hospital 1.09 vs 1.07, printed 1.06; ARDS 0.76 vs 0.86, printed 0.86 (0.59-1.24); pneumonia 1.15 vs 1.07, printed 1.07 (0.78-1.47); pneumothorax 1.37 vs 1.16, printed 1.16 (0.73-1.84); atelectasis 1.01 vs 1.01, printed 1.00; extrapulmonary infection 0.74 vs 0.84, printed 0.84 (0.60-1.18); sepsis 0.78 vs 0.87, printed 0.87 (0.56-1.33); delirium 1.19 vs 1.16, printed 1.15 (0.99-1.34); tracheostomy 1.05 vs 1.03, printed 1.03. Every printed RR and CI matches the transposed (allocation-given-outcome) ratio to within 0.01, and none matches the risk ratio of the stated percentages where the two differ. This is the pattern produced by passing a transposed 2x2 table to an RR routine. The card raised this as a diagnostic but did not adopt it; with all 10 rows matching I consider the issue confirmed. All RRs are biased toward 1 with too-narrow CIs; extractable values are wrong, so substantive/direct. Chi-square P values (recomputed) match printed values, so significance conclusions are unchanged.

rows.R: Protocol endpoint 'development of ARDS' (p.26) refers to the Berlin definition with mild/moderate/severe grades (Appendix p.48), but the daily data item is 'moderate or severe ARDS' (p.28). SAP p.9 and the article (pp.1,4,6) say 'new ARDS' (Berlin) without a severity threshold. Which grades were counted cannot be determined.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf pp.26,28,48; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.9; main pp.1,4,6 (text).
rows.rationale: The plan's collection item restricts to moderate/severe ARDS (PaO2/FiO2 <=200), whereas the endpoint and the report cite the full Berlin definition, which includes mild ARDS. If the report counted only collected events, its unqualified 'ARDS' outcome is narrower than its label; if mild cases were counted, it differs from the planned collection. The materials do not settle which, so L=indeterminate.

rows.R: Protocol pp.17-18 excludes PaO2/FiO2 <200 mm Hg unless the physician states no ARDS and no direct risk factor. SAP pp.6-7 and article p.2 list only clinical ARDS (Berlin) as the ARDS-related exclusion. Table 1 p.5: median baseline PaO2/FiO2 197 vs 195, so about half of patients were <200 at baseline.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf pp.17,18; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf pp.6,7; main pp.2,5; joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.9 (text).
rows.rationale: The protocol's oxygenation-based exclusion (with a narrow exception) does not appear in the SAP or the report. With baseline medians just below 200 in both arms, the enrolled population cannot have been limited as the protocol describes unless the exception was applied to about half of patients, which the report does not state. Eligibility differs, so substantive_difference.

rows.R: Protocol (summary p.10, power p.19, analysis p.33) defines VFD at day 28 'after ICU admission'; SAP p.8 'day 1 to day 28'; article p.4 counts from randomization. Randomization was required within 1 h of ICU ventilation/admission (median 0.57 h after ICU ventilation start, p.5), so the anchors differ by about an hour at most.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf pp.10,19,26,33; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf p.8; main pp.4,5,6 (text).
rows.rationale: A real difference in the stated time origin of the primary outcome, but by design randomization occurred within 1 hour of ICU admission or of the start of ICU ventilation, and VFD is counted in whole days. The practical difference in the outcome is negligible; minor_presentation.

rows.R: Protocol p.33: primary VFD analysed with Cox regression (power p.19 uses a t test). Updated SAP p.12 and article p.4: Student t test, mean difference. Disclosed: SAP modification table p.21 and article p.2 (updated SAP before database closure).
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf pp.19,33; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf pp.12,21,22; main pp.2,4,6 (text).
rows.rationale: The primary analysis method changed from Cox regression to a t test. The change is disclosed (updated SAP dated 24 Nov 2017, database locked 30 Dec 2017). Retained per the fixed decision with 'disclosed'. Different estimand (hazard ratio vs mean difference), so substantive_difference.

rows.R: Planned but not reported: per-protocol analysis (protocol p.33; SAP pp.13-14), respiratory-rate subgroup (SAP p.14 item 9; eTable 5 has 8 subgroups), covariate-adjusted zero-inflated GLM sensitivity (SAP pp.14-15), mediation analysis (SAP p.15). Only the GLMM sensitivity (P=.72, p.6) is reported. SAP matrix pp.21-22 partly discloses the omissions.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp1_prod.pdf p.33; joi180108supp2_prod.pdf pp.13-15,21,22; main pp.4,6,7; joi180108supp3_prod.pdf pp.1-13; joi180108supp4_prod.pdf p.1 (text).
rows.rationale: Searched the article and all results supplements: no per-protocol, covariate-adjusted, mediation or respiratory-rate subgroup result appears. The SAP's modification table states that the per-protocol analysis was 'not described' in the paper and that the covariate-adjusted GLM is not reported; disclosure in a supplement does not remove the difference. Several planned primary-outcome analyses are missing.

rows.R: SAP p.14: subgroup interactions by GLM with zero-inflated distributions and a forest plot. Article p.4 and eTable 5 p.9: Gaussian GLM, table only. Disclosed in SAP modification table p.22 as a post hoc change (CLT justification).
rows.evidence: joi180108supp2_prod.pdf pp.14,22; main pp.4,6; joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.9 (text, page rendered).
rows.rationale: The model for the prespecified subgroup analyses changed from zero-inflated to Gaussian, which changes the estimand and the interaction test. Disclosed in the supplement; retained per the fixed decision. Note outside the candidate: main text p.6 labels the subgroup 95% CIs as 'IQR'.

rows.R: eTable 2 p.6 (rendered), Other mode, after titration on randomization day, intermediate arm: PEEP '8 (5 - 1)'. An upper quartile of 1 below a median of 8 is impossible; most likely a dropped digit (e.g., 10). Descriptive cell for 28 patients.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.6 (text and 150-dpi render, crop viewed).
rows.rationale: Median 8 with IQR 5 to 1 violates Q1 <= median <= Q3; the render confirms the printed '1'. The intended value cannot be recovered with certainty. It is a descriptive ventilator setting in a small non-protocol mode subgroup and does not affect any outcome, so minor_presentation.

rows.R: eTable 5 p.9 (rendered): the two value rows for 'Ventilation before randomization' sit on the wrapped header line and the '>6 hours' line; the '<=6 hours' line is blank. CI widths (13.49 vs 3.00) imply roughly 21 vs 456 patients per arm, consistent with first row = >6 h (median ventilation before randomization 0.9 h), so attribution is recoverable.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp3_prod.pdf p.9 (rendered 150 dpi); main pp.4,5 (text); hand calculation.
rows.rationale: Half-width 6.745 gives SE 3.44; with SDs about 11, n per arm ≈ (11.6^2+10.7^2)/3.44^2 ≈ 21. For the second row, SE 0.765 gives n ≈ (11.6^2+11.5^2)/0.765^2 ≈ 456 per arm. 21+456 ≈ 477, the arm size, and only a few patients can have been ventilated >6 h before randomization under the 1-hour rule. A real layout misalignment, but the intended attribution can be inferred; P for interaction is unaffected. Also the footer reads 'Data are mean ()' while cells are mean ± SD.

rows.R: eTable 4 p.8 title 'during the first three days'; days of vasopressor use 2 (1-4) in both arms. eTable 2 (p.6) structures this period as randomization day plus days 1-3, i.e., four calendar days, so Q3=4 is compatible with calendar-day counting. No contradiction established.
rows.evidence: joi180108supp3_prod.pdf pp.5-8 (text); main pp.4,6.
rows.rationale: If exposure is counted in calendar days and the window comprises the randomization day plus days 1-3 (as eTables 1-3 tabulate it), a maximum of 4 days is possible and Q3=4 is admissible. The counting unit is not defined (sedative days are fractional, vasopressor days integer), but an undefined unit with a coherent reading is not an inconsistency between report statements. Exclude; the card itself notes the four-date reading is not impossible.

rows.R: PaO2:FIO2 150 vs 119 (difference 19.5, 4.4 to 34.6): abstract outcome list p.1 says 'over the 3 days after intubation'; main p.6 says 'significantly higher until day 4'; eTable p.2 gives 150 [104-230] vs 119 [86-165] as the value 6 h after randomization. Time origin (intubation vs randomization) and time point (6 h vs days 1-4) conflict.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf pp.1,3,6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf pp.1,2,4 (text).
rows.rationale: The same key-secondary numbers are tied to three different descriptions. The eTable is explicit (6 h after randomization) and its medians match 150/119, so the abstract's 'after intubation' window and the text's 'until day 4' framing misdescribe what the numbers are. A reader extracting the abstract would attach the effect to the wrong population (intubated patients) and period. Substantive.

rows.R: Final SAP pp.98-99: strata time since ICU admission D0-D2 vs >=D3, oxygen flow <9 vs >=9 L/min; interaction analyses on these strata. Article p.2 randomization uses <=2 vs >=3 days and >9 vs <=9 L/min; Figure 3 p.7 subgroups use ICU time 0-1 vs >=2 days and flow <=9 vs >9.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.98,99,104 (text); main pp.2,4,5,7 (text).
rows.rationale: The ICU-time subgroup cut point moved from 2/3 days (planned strata) to 1/2 days in the reported subgroup analysis, and patients at exactly 9 L/min change sides (planned <9 vs >=9; reported <=9 vs >9). The report calls these predefined subgroups. Subgroup membership changes, so substantive_difference.

rows.R: Final SAP p.99: 'HFNO will not be used in the control group.' Article p.3 permits HFNO in controls with do-not-intubate orders after standard-oxygen failure; p.5 reports 30 controls (7.7%) switched to HFNO. The report presents this as protocol, not as a deviation.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf p.99 (text); main pp.3,5 (text); Figure 1 p.3.
rows.rationale: The control intervention as reported includes a rescue allowance that the plan prohibits; 30 control patients received HFNO. This affects the contrast between arms (ITT dilution). Substantive difference in procedure.

rows.R: Final SAP p.103 secondary outcomes include dyspnea by VAS and Borg scale and oxygenation by lowest SpO2 and PaO2/FIO2 days 1-3 (also initial protocol pp.38,46; p.90 summary). Report gives dyspnea VAS only and PaO2/FIO2 only (pp.3,4,6; eFigs 2-3); no Borg scale or lowest-SpO2 result.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.38,46,90,103; main pp.1,3,4,6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf pp.1-5 (text).
rows.rationale: Searched all report materials (main and the 5-page supplement): no Borg-scale or lowest-SpO2 results. Planned measurement components of secondary outcomes are not reported.

rows.R: Final SAP p.104: primary binary outcome analysed as relative risk of death with 95% CI, plus analyses adjusted for potential confounders and a per-protocol analysis. Report pp.3-5: Kaplan-Meier, unadjusted Cox HR and risk difference; no RR, no adjusted analysis (limitation p.8 notes no adjustment for strata), no per-protocol analysis.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.53,54,82,104; main pp.3-8; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf pp.1-5 (text).
rows.rationale: Effect measure changed (RR to HR), planned adjusted and per-protocol analyses of the primary outcome are absent. The limitation acknowledges the lack of adjustment, which counts as disclosure but not removal of the difference.

rows.R: Final SAP p.105: intubation and ICU-acquired infection analysed as competing-risk outcomes with death or discharge alive as competitors, Gray test, cause-specific Cox for adjustment. Report: IMV with death without IMV as the only competitor (p.3); infection compared by chi-square (p.4) though Table 2 prints a cause-specific HR.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.54,82,105; main pp.3-6 (text).
rows.rationale: Competing event set differs for IMV (discharge alive not mentioned), and ICU-acquired infection is analysed by a chi-square test of proportions rather than as a competing-risk outcome; the Table 2 HR for infection is not described in the methods. Analysis method differs from plan.

rows.R: IMV cumulative incidence: methods p.4 say compared with the Gray test; eFigure 1 (supp2 p.3) labels 'P (log Rank test) = 0.17'; Table 2 p.5 and text p.6 attach P=.17 to the cause-specific HR. One P value, two test names.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf pp.3-6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf p.3 (text).
rows.rationale: The Gray test (comparing cumulative incidence functions) and the log-rank test (comparing cause-specific hazards) are different tests; the report attributes the same .17 to both. Which test produced it cannot be determined. The result is nonsignificant either way, so presentation-level.

rows.R: Table 1 p.4 (n=388 per arm): HF liver 45 (13.3) [45/388=11.6%], SO kidney 69 (20.4) [17.8%], HF postextubation 14 (4.1) [3.6%], SO postextubation 18 (5.3) [4.6%]. All four percentages reproduce with denominator 338 (13.3, 20.4, 4.1, 5.3); the other cells in the same rows use 388.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf p.4 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: 45/388=11.6, 45/338=13.3; 69/388=17.8, 69/338=20.4; 14/388=3.6, 14/338=4.1; 18/388=4.6, 18/338=5.3. No missing-data note for these variables, and the comparator cells in the same rows (e.g., SO liver 56 (14.4)=56/388) use 388, so a 338 denominator typo is the likely cause. Counts are presumably correct; baseline descriptors only.

rows.R: Original and final SAP (pp.55,82,105): oxygenation, dyspnea and comfort to be analysed with joint longitudinal models accounting for censoring. Report p.4: Wilcoxon rank-sum comparisons at time points; eFigures 2-3 show per-time-point data with marked significance; no joint-model result.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.55,82,105; main pp.1,4,6; joi180109supp2_prod.pdf pp.4,5 (text).
rows.rationale: The planned joint model (handling informative dropout from intubation/death/discharge, which the eFigure numbers at risk show is substantial) was replaced by cross-sectional rank tests. Method differs.

rows.R: Final SAP p.105: ICU length of stay analysed overall by Kaplan-Meier and separately in survivors and decedents by competing-risk estimators. Report p.4: Wilcoxon rank-sum; Table 2 gives medians and a difference 0.6 (-1.0 to 2.2), all patients combined.
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.54,82,105; main pp.1,4,5,6 (text).
rows.rationale: Neither the planned estimators nor the planned survivor/decedent populations appear in the report.

rows.R: Mortality in intubated patients was a secondary endpoint only in the initial grant protocol (noninferiority design, pp.6-7,38,45-47); the final SAP secondary list (p.103) omits it. The report labels it post hoc (p.6) and discloses the redesign (p.3). Consistent with the governing final plan.
rows.rationale: The supplement states that the initial protocol was the grant submission and that the final protocol/SAP governed (p.1, no amendments). Relative to the final plan the analysis is indeed not prespecified, so the report's post hoc label is accurate; the change occurred between plan versions before the trial, in a known sequence, and the report discloses the redesign. No plan-report difference against the governing plan; exclude. (A plan_material framing would also not fit, since the earlier protocol was superseded rather than conflicting.)

rows.R: Figure 3 p.7: every subgroup HR matches standard/high-flow, not high-flow/standard (e.g., IMV no hematologic malignancy 61/199 HF vs 89/198 SO, crude SO/HF ratio 1.47, printed HR 1.61), while headings place 'favors high-flow' left of 1. 'All patients' rows swap counts and invert Table 2 (deaths 140 vs 138; HR 1.02 vs 0.98; IMV 170 vs 150; HR 1.17 vs 0.85).
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf pp.4-7 (text); R crude-ratio comparison of all 26 rows.
rows.rationale: R crude risk ratios for 13 mortality and 13 IMV rows: in every row the printed HR is on the same side of 1 as the SO/HF ratio (e.g., mortality ICU >=2 days: SO/HF 1.41, HR 1.55; catecholamines yes: SO/HF 0.69, HR 0.62; IMV PaO2/FIO2 >=200: SO/HF 0.89, HR 0.88). Subgroup counts sum to Table 2 totals by column (138 and 140 deaths; 150 and 170 IMV), so the columns are labeled correctly, but the 'All patients' counts are swapped and the HRs are reciprocals of Table 2 (1/0.98=1.02; 1/0.85=1.18). With the favors labels as printed, the one significant subgroup (IMV, no hematologic malignancy, HR 1.61, interaction P=.01) reads as harm from high-flow oxygen when the counts show fewer intubations with high-flow (30.7% vs 44.9%). Substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 p.5 ICU-acquired infection 39 vs 41 of 388: cause-specific HR 1.01 (0.96 to 1.06). With 80 events the log-HR SE is about sqrt(1/39+1/41)=0.224, giving a CI near 0.61-1.47; the printed interval is roughly 10 times too narrow. RD -0.6 (-4.6 to 4.1) is also not centered (Wald -0.5, -4.8 to 3.8).
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf pp.4,5,6 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: Whatever the competing-risk handling, a cause-specific Cox model on 80 events cannot give a 95% CI of width 0.10 on the HR scale; the companion HRs for mortality (278 events, 0.77-1.24) and IMV (320 events, 0.68-1.06) are far wider. The point estimate 1.01 alongside fewer events in the HF arm is also odd. The printed interval is not reproducible and would be extracted; substantive. Outside the candidate: ICU and hospital mortality P values (.64, .77) do not match chi-square tests of the counts (R: .94, .88).

rows.R: Main p.6: 'vasopressors and renal replacement therapy were needed in 153 patients (19.7%) randomized to high-flow ... and 31 patients (4%) randomized to standard oxygen ..., with no statistical difference'. 153/776=19.7% and 31/776=4.0% (pooled), not 153/388=39.4% or 31/388=8.0%; 153 vs 31 of 388 each could not be nonsignificant.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf pp.3,5,6 (text); hand recomputation.
rows.rationale: The percentages use the pooled 776 denominator while the sentence attributes counts to arms, and the 'no statistical difference' claim is incompatible with arm-specific counts of 153 vs 31. The most likely reading is pooled counts for two separate therapies (vasopressors 153, RRT 31) with arm labels attached in error, but the paragraph cannot be read reliably. Arm-specific use of these therapies cannot be extracted.

rows.R: Figure 3 p.7 subgroup totals: PaO2:FIO2 <200/>=200 = 237+65=302 (HF) and 251+35=286 (SO); hematologic malignancy No/Yes = 199+167=366 and 198+181=379, vs 388 per arm. Table 1 gives 167/181 with malignancy, so 'No' should be 221/207. Other subgroups sum to 388. Methods p.3: no participants excluded for missing data.
rows.evidence: jama_azoulay_2018_oi_180109.pdf pp.3,4,7 (text).
rows.rationale: Missing PaO2:FIO2 at baseline is plausible (no arterial gas) but not reported. Hematologic malignancy is a recorded baseline characteristic with no reason to be missing; 22 HF and 9 SO patients are unaccounted for. The unqualified statement that no participant was excluded for missing data conflicts with these totals. Probable rather than confirmed because a restricted 'No' category could be intended. Subgroup HRs remain interpretable; denominators are unexplained.

rows.R: Figure 3 title p.7 calls all subgroups 'predefined', and methods p.4 say subgroups were defined by stratification variables, but the unknown-diagnosis and hematologic-malignancy subgroups appear in neither the initial protocol (pp.45-46: PaO2/FIO2, organ dysfunction, intubated, post-extubation, DNI) nor the final SAP strata (pp.98-99,104).
rows.evidence: joi180109supp1_prod.pdf pp.45,46,53,82,98,99,104 (text search for subgroup terms); main pp.4,7 (text).
rows.rationale: Two of the seven displayed subgroup factors have no prospective specification in any supplied plan version, yet are labeled predefined. One of them yields the only significant interaction (IMV, P=.01). Claim of prespecification without plan basis; substantive_difference.

rows.R: Report (abstract p.1; p.3) says temperature was managed in both groups for 7 days. Final protocol v9 §12.11 (p.77) and Appendix F (p.101): control-arm pyrexia avoidance only up to 96 h after randomization, then unit protocol; post-rewarming normothermia 'up to 7 days' (p.77) but '96 hours' (p.101).
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.1,3; joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.77,89,101 (text).
rows.rationale: For the control arm the plan limits protocolized temperature management to 96 h; the report states 7 days for both groups. The plan is itself inconsistent for the hypothermia arm (7 days vs 96 h). The control-arm co-intervention window differs between plan and report.

rows.R: Abstract p.1: 'risk difference, 0.4% [95% CI, -9.4% to 8.7%]'; main p.5 and Table 2 p.7: -0.4 (-9.4 to 8.7). 117/240 vs 111/226 gives RD -0.4 (-9.4 to 8.7), RR 0.99 (0.82-1.19), P=.94. The abstract drops the minus sign.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.1,5,7 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: 48.75% - 49.12% = -0.37, Wald CI -9.4 to 8.7; chi-square P=0.94. The abstract point estimate has the wrong sign; the CI and the body are correct. The difference is tiny and nonsignificant, so interpretation is unchanged, but an extractor using the abstract would take +0.4.

rows.R: Report p.3: 33°C maintained for at least 72 h after randomization; rewarming assessed at 72 h. Plan anchors differ: synopsis §6.5 (p.69) 'a further 72 hours' after reaching 33°C; Appendix F (p.97) 72 h 'after severe head injury'; §12.11 and flowchart (pp.77,99) 72 h after randomisation with a 48-h minimum if cooling started late. Report matches the operative rewarming rule but omits the late-start minimum.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.3,4; joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.69,77,97,99 (text).
rows.rationale: The plan uses three different anchors; the report adopts the one used in the operative rewarming section and flowchart. The 48-h minimum for late starters is not mentioned in the report. The planned and reported conduct are clear from the flowchart; the difference is mainly in description. minor_presentation.

rows.R: Report p.3: rewarming 'at a target rate up to 0.25°C/h'. Final protocol v9 §12.11 (p.77) and Appendix F (pp.99-100): 0.17°C/h (0.5°C every 3 h, max). The 0.25°C/h figure is from protocol v1 (2009, p.21). Reported median rewarming 22.5 h (p.4) fits about 0.17°C/h.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.3,4; joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.21,77,99,100 (text).
rows.rationale: The described rewarming rate is the superseded v1 value. From 33°C to 37°C in a median 22.5 h is 4/22.5 = 0.18°C/h, consistent with the final protocol's 0.17°C/h, so the conduct appears to follow the final plan and the discrepancy is in the description.

rows.R: Protocol v8 amendment (pp.174-175) and v9 §15.2 (p.84): modified ITT excludes consent withdrawals and patients not fulfilling inclusion criteria who never received the intervention. Report p.3: a priori analyses by randomized group excluding only consent withdrawals; ineligible patients are excluded only from PP/AS-treated (p.4; supp2 pp.12,17).
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.84,174,175 (text); main pp.3,4; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf pp.12,17 (text).
rows.rationale: The primary analysis population differs from the amended plan: the report's ITT retains ineligible never-treated patients that the protocol's modified ITT would exclude. The number affected is not reported. Population definition for the primary analysis differs.

rows.R: Protocol v9 §15.2 (p.84): primary outcome reported as RR, RD and OR, each with 95% CI. Report (pp.1,3,5,7) gives RR and RD only; the only primary-outcome ORs are in the post hoc adequate-cooling analysis (supp2 p.22). No ITT primary OR in the main text or supp2 pp.1-24.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.84; main pp.1,3,5,7; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf pp.1-24 (text search).
rows.rationale: One of three planned effect measures for the primary analysis is not reported. The same 2x2 data are fully given (117/240 vs 111/226; crude OR computable as 0.98), so the omission is presentational.

rows.R: Methods p.4: survival censored at 6 months; data collection p.2: follow-up to death or 6 months. eFigure 2 (supp2 p.5, rendered) plots survival to 250 days with 23 and 17 still at risk at day 250, and n=260/240 at time 0 (6-month mortality analysis n=256/239). Caption: probability of death at 6 months; HR 1.13 (0.76-1.69).
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.2,4,5; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.5 (text and 110-dpi render).
rows.rationale: The plotted window extends well beyond the stated 6-month censoring, so the displayed KM curve (and possibly the HR) does not use the stated analysis window. Curves are flat after about day 100, so the HR is unlikely to change materially. The risk-set denominators also differ from the 6-month mortality denominators.

rows.R: eTable 7 (supp2 p.11): favorable outcome by time to 33°C 18/49, 28/67, 32/59, 39/65 (never), P=.09; methods p.4 specify a chi-square test for equal proportions; main p.5 reports no significant difference. R: 4-group chi-square P=.043 (Fisher .044); 3 groups excluding 'never' P=.16; trend tests .005 (4 groups) and .064 (3 groups). None gives .09.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.4,5; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.11 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: Under the stated test across all four displayed categories the P value is 0.043, below .05, which would contradict the text's 'not significantly different'. The test that produced .09 cannot be identified; an unstated variant (e.g., another grouping) could explain it, hence probable rather than confirmed. The comparison is post-randomization and confounded, but the significance statement is what is reported, so substantive.

rows.R: Final protocol v9 §15.1.3 (p.84, July 2017): with 11 interim looks the final analysis uses ±1.996 SD (P=0.0459). DSMC charter transcription (p.188): final critical value 1.975 (P .048) but 'all final analyses were conducted with alpha 0.05'. Report p.4: 2-sided P<.05.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.84,188 (text); main p.4.
rows.rationale: The latest protocol specifies a final significance threshold of 0.0459; the report uses 0.05, matching the charter text. The charter is described as the 2015 charter but is transcribed in past tense, so which document governed the final rule cannot be resolved from the materials. The primary P=.94 means no conclusion depends on it.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 bleeding rows have RR/CI/P swapped. Intracranial 47/260 vs 37/240: RR 1.17 (0.79-1.74), P=.43; printed 1.23 (0.43-3.5), P=.70. Extracranial 8/260 vs 6/240: RR 1.23 (0.43-3.50), P=.70; printed 1.17 (0.79-1.74), P=.43. eTable 6 (supp2 p.10) gives the correct P values (.43, .70). RDs are correct.
rows.evidence: jama_cooper_2018_oi_180132.pdf pp.1,3,5,7; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.10 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R log-RR Wald and chi-square: intracranial RR 1.17 (0.79-1.74), P 0.43; extracranial RR 1.23 (0.43-3.50), P 0.70. All other Table 2 rows reproduce exactly. The triplets are exchanged between the two bleeding rows, giving intracranial bleeding (the clinically important safety outcome) a spuriously wide CI. Extractable values wrong; substantive.

rows.R: Interim rule |Z|>=3 (Haybittle-Peto 3 SD) is attached to different P thresholds in plan documents: 2010 amendment (p.152, rendered; scanned and rotated) 'P<0.005'; DSMC charter (p.188) 'approximate P <0.001'; final protocol p.84 states 3SD without a P. Two-sided P at |Z|=3 is 0.0027.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf p.152 (rendered 130 dpi; OCR garbled by rotation), pp.84,188 (text); hand calculation.
rows.rationale: 2*(1-pnorm(3)) = 0.0027 (one-sided 0.00135). 'P<0.005' is a loose but true bound; 'approximately P<0.001' understates the two-sided P. The operative boundary (|Z|>=3) is stated consistently in all versions, so the P-value glosses are a presentational inconsistency; no stopping decision depended on them.

rows.R: DSMB report July 2016 (supp1 pp.191-192, rendered): block favorable counts for Y sum to 73 (7,2,11,5,8,6,3,5,6,5,2,4,3,6), matching the table (GROUPy 73), but the cumulative Y line runs 6,12,17,...,80. The X cumulative line (10,18,...,86) matches its blocks.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.191,192 (text and 110-dpi renders).
rows.rationale: Cumulative sums of the printed Y block numerators: 7, 9, 20, 25, 33, 39, 42, 47, 53, 58, 60, 64, 67, 73. The plotted Y series does not follow these and ends at 80, inconsistent with the 73 in the same report. Internal interim (blinded-arm) DSMB display; no effect on the final results.

rows.R: eTable 10 (supp2 p.18) as-treated baseline, normothermia (n=196), evacuated mass lesion V printed '34.7 (68)': count and percentage transposed (68/196 = 34.7%). Same table: nonevacuated VI '1 (2)' where 1/196 = 0.5%.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.18 (text).
rows.rationale: 68/196 = 0.347, so the intended cell is 68 (34.7). The adjacent '1 (2)' cell is also inconsistent with n=196 (0.5%). Baseline descriptors in a sensitivity population; intended values recoverable.

rows.R: Supp2 p.22 (rendered): 'adjusted odds ratio ... 0.95 (0.55-275 1.64) P = .84'. A stray '275' sits inside the CI; the intended interval is evidently 0.55-1.64. Unadjusted OR 58/124 vs 111/226 = 0.91 reproduces.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp2_prod.pdf p.22 (text and 110-dpi render, crop viewed).
rows.rationale: The render confirms the printed token. 0.95 lies within 0.55-1.64 and the CI is roughly symmetric on the log scale (log 0.55=-0.60, log 1.64=0.49, centre -0.05 ≈ log 0.95), so 1.64 is the upper limit and '275' is an artifact (likely a line number). Unadjusted OR check: (58*115)/(66*111) = 0.91. Typographic.

rows.R: Protocol v9 p.85: sensitivity analyses of primary and secondary outcomes adjusted for prespecified baseline covariates and any imbalanced covariate. SAP update (pp.183-184,187; scanned, OCR'd) restricts PP/as-treated adjustment to IMPACT-TBI. Report gives an IMPACT-adjusted RR for the primary outcome only (Table 2); no adjusted results for mortality or adverse events.
rows.evidence: joi180132supp1_prod.pdf pp.84,85,181 (text), 183,184,187 (OCR 250 dpi); main pp.1,3-7; joi180132supp2_prod.pdf (text search).
rows.rationale: The planned covariate-adjusted sensitivity analyses of secondary outcomes are not reported. The published SAP (Trials 2018) is cited but not supplied in full (p.181 gives only the citation), so its exact covariate list could not be checked; the protocol text alone establishes the plan.

rows.R: Abstract p.1: '22% men'. Main p.4: 22 men and 8 women of 30 enrolled = 73.3% men; eTable 2 (supp2 pp.3-4) lists 22 male and 8 female patients. The abstract percentage is wrong (22 is the count; women are 26.7%).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.1,4; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf pp.3,4 (text).
rows.rationale: 22/30 = 73.3%; 8/30 = 26.7%. The abstract reports the sex distribution essentially inverted. Sex composition is a routinely extracted baseline characteristic and the abstract value is grossly wrong, so substantive.

rows.R: Protocol pp.12,40-41: hierarchical model with patient random intercept and slope, elicited clinical priors (e.g., mean effect N(1.75, 0.89)) for main parameters, inverse-gamma(0.001,0.001) variance priors, and a robustness comparison with noninformative priors. Report (p.3; eMethods 1-3, supp2 pp.10-14): vague normal priors on period means, uniform(0.01,10) SDs; no clinical-prior analysis or robustness comparison.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf pp.12,40,41 (text); main pp.3,4,6; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf pp.10-14 (text).
rows.rationale: The planned primary Bayesian analysis with elicited clinical priors and the planned prior-sensitivity comparison are not reported; the model structure and variance priors also differ. Primary-analysis specification differs.

rows.R: Protocol p.40: secondary endpoints 'analyzed in the same way' (Bayesian hierarchical model). Report p.3 and Table 2 (pp.7-8): non-IVR secondary outcomes analysed with frequentist dependent t tests and genotype interaction tests; Bayesian results only for IVR scores.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf pp.7,31,40 (text); main pp.3,4,7,8 (text and 200-dpi render).
rows.rationale: Analysis framework for the non-IVR secondary outcomes changed from Bayesian hierarchical to frequentist paired tests. Analysis method differs.

rows.R: Protocol pp.32-33: eye closure and handgrip myotonia after 3-s contractions; dynamometry relaxation measured as 90%-10%, 90%-50% and 90%-75% of MVIC, three sets. Report p.3 and Table 2 fn h/j: 5-s contractions; relaxation 90%-5% only; adds peak force and transient paresis.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf pp.32,33 (text); main pp.3,5,7,8 (text and render).
rows.rationale: Bedside test procedure (3 s vs 5 s) and the dynamometry relaxation endpoint (three planned windows vs one unplanned 90%-5% window) differ. Measurement definitions of secondary outcomes changed.

rows.R: Protocol p.35: intent-to-treat; all data acquired before termination included in the primary analysis unless consent withdrawn. Report: 27 completers analysed (Figure 1 p.4; eTable 3 excludes dropouts 3, 6, 7); p.3 states patients completing at least one treatment period were included.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.35 (text); main pp.3,4,8; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.5 (text).
rows.rationale: Three randomized patients (two nonadherent, one SAE) contribute no data to the aggregated analysis, whereas the plan includes pre-withdrawal data. Whether they had any complete period is not stated, but they are explicitly excluded from the primary analysis set. Analysis population differs.

rows.R: Protocol p.40: investigate interactions between treatment effect and treatment pair, and treatment effect and treatment order, in the Bayesian model. Report p.3-4: frequentist candidate covariables 'randomization order' and 'period effect' (P=.85, .22) dropped from the model; no Bayesian interaction result.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.40 (text); main pp.3,4; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf pp.10-14 (text).
rows.rationale: The report gives order and period terms in the frequentist model, which may correspond to the planned treatment-by-order (carryover) and treatment-by-pair checks, but they are described as covariables, not interactions, and are not from the planned Bayesian model. Whether the planned analysis was done in another form cannot be determined.

rows.R: Main p.4: 'In 3 patients (11%), Bayesian analysis showed the predefined clinical ineffectiveness' (posterior <20%). eTable 3 (supp2 p.5): patients 13 (2%) and 22 (1%) meet it; patient 11 had 38% and was stopped because stiffness was absent in both periods (footnote). Also patients 8 and 20 at exactly 80% are counted as responders under the reported '>80%' rule.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.1,3,4; joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.5 (text); joi180136supp1_prod.pdf p.42.
rows.rationale: Only 2 of the 3 reported nonresponders met the stated Bayesian criterion; the third was a clinical decision disclosed only in the supplement footnote. Related: the article and eTable 3 define responders as posterior >80%, but patients 8 and 20 have exactly 80% (the protocol p.42 says 'at least 80%', so they meet the plan's rule but not the reported one). The headline 24/3 split thus does not follow from the rule as reported. Substantive for the individual-level result.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5: INQoL composite median (IQR) 84.0 (74.5-110.3) and 98.0 (56.0-120.0), but footnote f (and Table 2 fn g) give the scale as 0-100. Upper quartiles 110.3 and 120.0 exceed the stated maximum; Table 2 baseline mean 96.89 (SD 38.49) is also implausible on a 0-100 scale.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.3,5,7,8 (text and render).
rows.rationale: Values above 100 cannot occur on a 0-100 scale, so either the stated range or the scoring/values are wrong. Which is wrong cannot be determined: if a different (unbounded or summed) scoring was used, the INQoL treatment effect (-14.22) is on an unstated scale. Hence substantiveness indeterminate.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5 'Other' pretrial medication 7/16 (44%) vs 5/11 (46%), P=.62. Fisher exact P=1.00 (chi-square .93); the adjacent rows reproduce with Fisher (men 13/16 vs 7/11 P=.39; mexiletine 2/16 vs 0/11 P=.50). Footnote a says Mann-Whitney (computed .95). 5/11 = 45.5%.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf p.5 (text and render); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: Fisher .391 and .499 match the printed .39 and .50 for the adjacent rows; for the Other row Fisher 1.000, chi-square .930, Mann-Whitney .954; none gives .62. Baseline descriptive P value; no inference depends on it.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 (render) and text p.6: SCN4A fifth transient paresis effect 13.71 (-1.96 to 25.47), P=.02. The CI crosses 0 while P<.05 and is not centred on 13.71; with lower limit +1.96 the CI is centred (13.715) and P≈.02. Likely a spurious minus sign.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.4,6,7,8 (text and 200-dpi render); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: printed CI implies P≈.050; with +1.96 lower limit, P≈.02 (normal/t). The printed interval contradicts the printed P, and is repeated in the text. This SCN4A effect (worse transient paresis on mexiletine, period means -5.00 vs +9.56) is significant and favors placebo, which also contradicts footnote d ('All statistically significant findings favored mexiletine'). Extractable CI wrong; substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 lower section (p.7) header 'Treatment Effect (Placebo-Mexiletine)', but values equal mexiletine minus placebo change: SF-36 physical 8.66-1.04=+7.62 (printed +7.81); INQoL -21.44-(-7.22)=-14.22 (printed -14.22); first handgrip -2.39-0.46=-2.85 (printed -2.85). The upper IVR section is placebo minus mexiletine (5.55-2.42=3.12).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.7,8 (200-dpi render).
rows.rationale: Every lower-section effect has the sign of mexiletine minus placebo, opposite to the header and opposite to the convention of the upper section of the same table. Positive SF-36 effects and negative relaxation-time effects both favor mexiletine, so the direction of benefit is correctly readable only from the period columns. An extractor applying the header would reverse 27 effect estimates; substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7: SF-36 physical placebo change 1.04 (-0.60 to 2.96). The interval midpoint is 1.18, not 1.04; a symmetric t interval around 1.04 with upper 2.96 would have lower -0.88. Other period CIs in the table are centred on their means.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.3,7,8 (render); hand calculation.
rows.rationale: (-0.60+2.96)/2 = 1.18 vs 1.04, a 0.14 discrepancy beyond 2-decimal rounding. One limit is mistyped. Placebo-period change descriptor; inference concerns the treatment effect.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7: SF-36 mental treatment effect 6.78 (1.64 to 11.92), P=.001. A dependent t test with this CI implies P≈.012 (df 26) or .010 (normal). Printed .001 is about 10 times too small.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.3,4,7,8 (render); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: SE = 10.28/(2*2.056) = 2.50; t = 2.71; P = .012 (df 26), .0115 (df 30), .0097 (normal). Methods say dependent t tests for normally distributed outcomes, which leaves a small possibility that another test produced the P; hence probable. Significance at .05 is unchanged.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 (render): first handgrip placebo change 0.46 (-0.30 to -1.23): the mean lies outside its interval and the limits descend. With upper limit +1.23 the interval is centred at 0.465; a dropped/added minus sign.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.7,8 (200-dpi render).
rows.rationale: (-0.30+1.23)/2 = 0.465 ≈ 0.46. Typographic sign error in a placebo-period descriptor; the treatment effect (-2.85) reproduces as -2.39-0.46.

rows.R: Lower Table 2 effects vs difference of period mean changes: many rows match (INQoL, handgrip, eyelid, TUG), but several do not: SF-36 physical 7.62 vs 7.81, mental 6.62 vs 6.78, CLCN1 fifth handgrip -0.29 vs 0.04, peak force first 26.73 vs 32.92, fifth 21.81 vs 24.08, mean 33.75 vs 37.23, transient paresis first -3.09 vs -3.7, fifth -9.29 vs -12.25, mean -6.30 vs -7.34.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.3,4,7,8 (render); hand calculation for all lower rows.
rows.rationale: With a dependent t test on complete pairs and period means computed from all available data (report p.4: all available data; 98% of secondary measures collected; 31 sets from 27 patients), effects need not equal the difference of period means. Rows that reproduce exactly suggest the same population where data are complete, and the mismatches cluster in dynamometry outcomes, consistent with incomplete pairs. The CLCN1 fifth-handgrip row is harder to explain (effect 0.04 with CI -1.11 to 1.19, much wider than either period CI, and opposite in sign to -0.29). The materials do not allow a decision.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 and text p.8: SCN4A fifth handgrip effect -1.96 (-3.41 to 0.51), P=.009. CI crosses 0 while P<.05; with upper limit -0.51 the CI is centred exactly on -1.96 (P≈.01). Dropped minus sign.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.4,7,8 (render); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: (-3.41-0.51)/2 = -1.96. Printed CI implies P≈.05, contradicting P=.009 and the text's presentation of a significant genotype-specific effect. Extractable CI wrong and repeated in text; substantive.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7: first eyelid effect -4.25 (-8.45 to -0.05), P=.05. CI implies P=.047 (t, df 26-30), which rounds to .05; a CI just excluding 0 with P just under .05 is consistent. No conflict.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.4,7 (render); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: SE = 8.40/(2*2.056) = 2.04; t = 2.08; P = .0475. Two-digit rounding gives .05. The text (p.6) does not list first-eyelid among significant outcomes, which is slightly conservative but not contradictory. Exclude.

rows.R: Table 2 p.7 (render): Timed Up&Go mean, placebo change 0.07 (-0.67 to 0.01): mean exceeds the upper limit. With upper limit 0.81 the interval is centred at 0.07; likely a dropped digit.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.7,8 (200-dpi render).
rows.rationale: (-0.67+0.81)/2 = 0.07. Typographic error in a placebo-period descriptor; the treatment effect -1.12 = -1.05-0.07 reproduces.

rows.R: Table 2 p.8: needle-EMG grading effect 0.67 (0.23 to 1.11), P<.001. A dependent t test with this CI gives P≈.004 (df 26) or .003 (normal). The outcome is an ordinal 0-3 grade; methods (p.3) apply t tests to normally distributed outcomes, so another test may have produced the P.
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.3,4,8 (render); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R: SE = 0.88/(2*2.056) = 0.214; t = 3.13; P = .0043. The mismatch is real under the t test, but for an ordinal grade a nonparametric test is plausible and unstated. Cannot decide; significance unaffected either way.

rows.R: Protocol p.38: DSMB convenes if accumulated study-related serious adverse events are >=10% (three patients) or >=2 identical cardiac events. Figure 3 (p.39, rendered): convene if cardiac events (AE/SAE) occur in >10% (three patients) or >=2 identical cardiac events; any single cardiac event stops the individual trial.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf pp.38,39 (text and 110-dpi render).
rows.rationale: The text's population trigger counts any related SAE (>=10%); the figure counts cardiac events only and uses '>10%' (with 30 patients, >10% means >=4 rather than >=3). The two define different safety-monitoring triggers. It does not affect the reported efficacy analysis and no trigger was reached (one non-cardiac SAE), but the monitoring procedure itself is defined inconsistently.

rows.R: Protocol p.42: interim analyses use noninformative priors only. Figure 4 (p.43, rendered) shows '+ informative priors' feeding the LR1 and LR2 interim evaluations. The reported interim model (eMethods 1, supp2 p.10) uses vague priors, consistent with the text.
rows.evidence: joi180136supp1_prod.pdf pp.42,43 (text and 110-dpi render); joi180136supp2_prod.pdf p.10.
rows.rationale: The schematic contradicts the explicit text on the prior used for stopping advice. The text is specific and gives a rationale, and the figure is a generic diagram (it also uses likelihood-ratio labels not used elsewhere), so the intended rule is clear. Presentation-level inconsistency.

rows.R: Table 2 baseline means (N=27; CLCN1 16, SCN4A 11): fifth handgrip total 1.36 vs genotype-weighted (16*0.93+11*2.59)/27 = 1.61; fifth transient paresis 20.30 vs 18.15; mean transient paresis 24.11 vs 22.59. IVR stiffness reconciles (5.59 vs 5.65).
rows.evidence: jama_stunnenberg_2018_oi_180136.pdf pp.4,7,8 (render; card table consulted for row list); hand calculation.
rows.rationale: If the totals used all 30 enrolled patients, the 3 dropouts would need a negative fifth-handgrip relaxation sum to reconcile (30*1.36 = 40.8 < 43.4 from the genotype rows), which is impossible; and the implied genotype weights differ in opposite directions across rows (0.26 vs 0.73 CLCN1-equivalent). Different contributor sets per row could still explain part of it, so probable. Baseline descriptors only. Column C for this candidate has no file/page; locations taken from the card's evidence table.

rows.R: Protocol §5.1 (p.13): difficult-airway characteristics defining the primary population include facial or neck trauma, airway edema, blood or vomit. Report (pp.1,2,4; Table 3) and the data form (supp2 p.9 item 12): facial trauma only (no neck trauma), and adds airway obstruction (obstruction/edema).
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.13; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf pp.1,2,4,5,7; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf pp.7,9 (text).
rows.rationale: The criteria that define the primary analysis subgroup differ: neck trauma is dropped and airway obstruction is added. The postintubation form matches the report, so the implemented definition was probably fixed from the start, but it differs from the protocol. Membership of the primary analysis population can change; the number affected is not reported and is probably small.

rows.R: Protocol §4.1.1 (p.11): randomization strata = cervical collar, obesity, or apparent facial or neck trauma vs none. Report pp.2-3: strata = obesity or cervical immobilization vs neither; facial/neck trauma not mentioned.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.11; jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf pp.2,3,7 (text).
rows.rationale: One stratification factor (facial or neck trauma) is absent from the reported strata. Randomization procedure differs; the consequence is limited to balance (analyses are unstratified).

rows.R: Protocol §2.2/§3.2 (pp.9-10): hypoxemia ascertained from start of the first attempt until 1 min after ETT cuff inflation, SpO2 recorded every 20 s plus lowest value. Report (p.3; Table 3 fn b; Table 5 fn b): during or within 1 min after completion of the attempt (laryngoscope removal).
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf pp.9,10; main pp.1,3,7,9; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.2 (text).
rows.rationale: End anchors differ (cuff inflation vs blade removal), which for successful attempts are seconds apart; the 1-minute window and the threshold definition are the same. Minor difference in description.

rows.R: Protocol §2.2(2) (p.9): time to intubation from start of attempt to ETT cuff inflation with the tube in the trachea (successful intubations). Report (pp.3,4; Table 3 fn c): first-attempt duration from blade insertion to blade removal, for all first attempts including failures; KM 'time until first-attempt success'.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf pp.9,10,19; main pp.1,3,4,5,7,8 (text).
rows.rationale: The endpoint's end point and population differ: planned time to successful intubation vs reported blade-in-mouth duration of any first attempt. The report also adds a post hoc successful-attempt-only analysis. Outcome definition changed.

rows.R: Protocol §8.2 (p.19): enrol for 1 calendar year or until 1000 patients; if <374 difficult-airway patients by then, discuss extension with the IRB. Report p.3: trial stopped when more than 374 difficult-airway patients were enrolled (380 of 757), September 2016-August 2017.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf p.19; main pp.1,2,3,4,7 (text).
rows.rationale: The stated stopping trigger differs (subgroup accrual vs calendar year/1000 patients). Enrollment ran about 12 months, so the planned calendar rule and the reported accrual rule may have been met at about the same time; which rule actually governed cannot be determined.

rows.R: Protocol §8.1 (p.19): time-to-event data summarized by Kaplan-Meier 25th/50th/75th percentiles with 95% CIs and percentage censored. Report: KM curves (Figure 2, eFigure 1), log-rank, Cox HR; durations summarized as median (IQR) of observed times; no KM percentiles with CIs or censoring proportions.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf pp.9,19; main pp.1,4,5,7,8; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf pp.2-3 (text).
rows.rationale: Planned descriptive KM summaries are not given; the comparative KM analysis is. Descriptive presentation difference.

rows.R: Table 1 p.5: SpO2 <90% 44/352 and 40/344; <80% 21/352, 11/344. Footnote b: SpO2 missing for 19 (bougie) and 24 (ETT), implying denominators 362 and 352. Denominators do not match the stated missingness (10 and 8 extra missing).
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.5 (text); hand calculation.
rows.rationale: 381-19 = 362; 376-24 = 352. The printed denominators 352/344 imply 29 and 32 missing. Unresolvable from the table; baseline descriptors only (percentages change by <1 point).

rows.R: Table 1 p.5 nested medical indications mix denominators: altered mental status 185 (49) = 185/381; cardiac arrest 32 (8) = /381; but 'Asthma, COPD...' 16 (5) = 16/318 (16/381 = 4.2%) and Other 44 (14) = 44/318 (11.5% of 381); ETT arm 23 (7) and 41 (13) = /315.
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf p.5 (text); hand calculation.
rows.rationale: Counts sum correctly (185+32+21+20+16+44 = 318), but two rows use the medical subtotal as denominator while the others use the arm total, without labeling. Baseline descriptors; values recoverable from counts.

rows.R: Table 2 p.6: senior resident -5 (-10 to 0), P=.03; junior resident 5 (0 to 10), .03; screen during passage -6 (-12 to 0), .04. Wald CIs are -10.3 to -0.5, 0.4 to 9.8, -12.5 to -0.4; chi-square P .033, .033, .036. The '0' limits are integer rounding of limits that exclude 0. Consistent.
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf pp.4,6 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: R recomputation reproduces all three rows; the apparent touching of 0 is a display-precision artifact (whole-percent rounding). Exclude.

rows.R: Table 3 p.7, all-patient first-attempt duration difference '1 (4 to -1)': limits reversed. eTable 1 (supp2 p.2) gives 1 s (-1 s to 4 s).
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf pp.4,7; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf pp.2,3 (text).
rows.rationale: Order of limits inverted; the supplement shows the intended interval. Typographic.

rows.R: Table 3 p.7 Cormack-Lehane grade 4: 3/3 vs 2/5, difference 60 (17 to 100), P=.09. Wald CI 17.1 to 102.9 (truncated) excludes 0; uncorrected chi-square P=.090 (Fisher .196). The CI and P give opposite readings because both methods are unreliable with n=3 and 5 and a 100% cell.
rows.evidence: jama_driver_2018_oi_180054.pdf pp.4,6,7 (text); R recomputation.
rows.rationale: Each number reproduces under its stated method, but the Wald interval (zero variance in one arm) and the chi-square test are both invalid at these counts and contradict each other. An exact interval would include 0, consistent with Fisher P=.20. Exploratory 8-patient subgroup.

rows.R: Protocol §8.6.1 (pp.20-21): for the primary outcome, if both data forms are missing, video is reviewed 'to determine if first pass success without hypoxemia was achieved', which is the secondary outcome; the primary outcome (§2.1, pp.8-9) is first pass success.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf pp.8,9,20,21 (text).
rows.rationale: The missing-data clause for the primary outcome names a different (composite secondary) target. The heading and context make clear the primary outcome is meant; the report states no outcome data were missing for the primary analysis. Wording slip within the plan.

rows.R: Protocol §8.4.1/8.5/8.6.2 (pp.20-21): interim after 500 patients on the primary outcome, defined for the difficult-airway subgroup. eAppendix 1 (supp2 p.6): interim at 507 patients reports first-pass success in all patients (250/257 vs 213/250) and states the trial was continued, without the planned projection result or the difficult-airway subgroup.
rows.evidence: joi180054supp1_prod.pdf pp.20,21; joi180054supp2_prod.pdf p.6; main pp.3,4 (text).
rows.rationale: The interim population (all patients) differs from the primary analysis population the plan names, and the futility projection itself is not shown. Interim analysis conduct differs from plan.

rows.R: Protocol p.16 (and baseline survey, supp2 p.2): composite = total interventions performed among eligible patients / total possible interventions (opportunity-pooled). Report p.3: composite calculated for each patient and then averaged (patient-weighted); Table 2 reports mean (SD) 88.2 vs 84.8 and RD 3.5. The OR_PA model remains opportunity-based as planned (protocol pp.18-19; report p.4).
rows.evidence: joi180070supp1_prod.pdf pp.16,18,19; joi180070supp2_prod.pdf p.2; jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf pp.1,3,4,7 (text).
rows.rationale: The co-primary composite's weighting changed from pooling care opportunities (patients with more eligible measures weigh more) to averaging per-patient proportions. The two can differ, and the reported percentages and absolute difference use the new definition while the odds ratio uses the planned one. Primary outcome definition differs.

rows.R: Figure 1 p.5 (rendered) labels 2003 (intervention) and 1977 (control) patients, i.e., 12-month completers, as 'included in primary analysis'. Text p.4 states all 4800 patients were included in the primary analysis, and Table 2 uses 2400/2400 for the all-or-none measure.
rows.evidence: jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf pp.1,4,5,7 (text and 150-dpi render).
rows.rationale: 2400-397 = 2003 and 2400-423 = 1977 reconcile, so the boxes count follow-up completers, but they are labeled as the primary analysis population. The primary outcome (in-hospital adherence) was analysed in all 4800 per text and Table 2. The figure mislabels the analysis set; the correct population is stated elsewhere.

rows.R: Main p.5 Clinical Events: outcomes 'at 3, 6, and 12 months after discharge'. Methods p.3-4, Table 3 fn b (p.8), Figure 2 axes ('Days After Stroke Symptom Onset') and protocol p.16: after initial symptom onset. Median length of stay is 12-13 days (Table 1).
rows.evidence: jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf pp.3,4,5,6,8 (text); joi180070supp1_prod.pdf pp.16,19.
rows.rationale: One sentence uses discharge as origin; all definitional statements, the table footnote and the figure axes use symptom onset. The intended origin is clear; the discrepancy (about 2 weeks) is a wording slip.

rows.R: Table 3 p.8 in-hospital death 11/2400 vs 23/2400: adjusted difference -0.7 (-1.1 to 0.2), P=.009. The CI includes 0 while P<.01, and is not centred on -0.7; with upper limit -0.2 it is centred (-0.65) and gives P≈.005. Text p.5 says in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly; HR 0.96 (0.90-1.02), P=.14 in the same row.
rows.evidence: jama_wang_2018_oi_180070.pdf pp.4,5,8 (text); hand recomputation.
rows.rationale: Crude Wald: -0.50 (-0.97 to -0.03), P≈.036. Printed adjusted CI and P conflict; a dropped minus sign on the upper limit is the likely cause, but then the RD would be significant while the text calls in-hospital mortality nonsignificant. Also, an HR CI of 0.90-1.02 is implausibly narrow for 34 events (log-HR SE would be about 0.35), and 0.96 is far from the crude ratio of about 0.48. Which inference is correct cannot be determined; the row is internally inconsistent on a secondary mortality outcome.

rows.R: eTable 3 (supp2 p.6) 3-month vascular death -1.43 (-2.33 to -0.54), P=0.001. The CI implies z≈3.1-3.2, P≈.0016-.0019 across display-precision bounds, i.e., '.002' if rounded, '.001' if truncated. Other rows reproduce. Immaterial difference; no inferential conflict.
